children: will continue to make varying price cuts for diesel and heating fuel in France through the winter, as it participates in a government-led release of strategic diesel reserves to further ease consumer costs, CEO Patrick Pouyanne said Monday, according to Bloomberg.

The company, which has already spent ~€500M to cap prices at its French services stations, "will aim to remain the cheapest retail network in France, maybe even beyond the crisis," the CEO said after a meeting between the government and fuel retailers in Paris, acknowledging that its domestic service stations have gained market share due to its price cap.

Governments around the world have been seeking to ease a cost-of-living crisis as prices for diesel and crude oil have surged due to disruptions to flows through the Strait of Hormuz and Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries.
Amid a jump in refining margins, TotalEnergies
may pay ~€600M in taxes on corporate profits in France in 2026, Pouyanne also said.

title: TotalEnergies' CEO pledges more price cuts in France to ease diesel pain
